problem: Latent world models for MPC such as DINO-WM are trained with single-step teacher forcing but planned with multi-step autoregressive rollouts, and their cosine goal-distance cost is not guaranteed to rank candidate action sequences correctly, which misleads sampling-based planners like CEM.
motivation: Image-goal navigation with world models needs not only accurate prediction but also a planning cost that orders action sequences reliably. Train/test rollout mismatch and non-monotone cost surfaces (local minima) make CEM converge to poor plans even when the predictor is locally accurate.
key_idea: Train a frozen-DINO latent world model with an autoregressive rollout loss (with a counter-curriculum) and a Monotone Cost Ranking margin loss so the cosine goal cost rises with trajectory deviation, making CEM planning reliable.
insight: Rollout training beats teacher forcing on both encoders (DINOv2 AOE 9.12 vs 12.10 before MCR), and MCR gives the largest, most consistent gain (DINOv2 AOE 7.63 vs 9.12), so cost-landscape shaping matters as much as prediction accuracy. Order-sensitive InfoNCE with temporal-permutation negatives distorts latent geometry and degrades planning (DINOv3 AOE 21.17, DINO-WM level), and MCR only partially repairs it (11.92), showing that discriminative and geometry-preserving objectives conflict when the latent space is used directly as a cost.
method: Frozen DINO encoder: DINOv2-ViT-S/14 or DINOv3-ViT-S/16 patch features, layer-normalized; only the predictor is trained.

AdaLN ViT predictor: 6-layer causal ViT with RoPE (dim 384, 12 heads); an MLP maps the 4-D SE(2) action (dx, dy, sin dθ, cos dθ) to AdaLN scale/shift, instead of DINO-WM's per-patch action concatenation.

Autoregressive rollout loss: unroll K steps from a length-S ground-truth seed on the model's own outputs, with L2 + 0.5*cosine per-step loss; counter-curriculum ramps K from 2 to 8 over 18k steps while annealing LR and batch size.

Monotone Cost Ranking (MCR): 1k-step phase on the Base checkpoint; GT actions perturbed with AR(1) noise at σ∈{0.05,0.15,0.35}; a pairwise margin-ranking loss (margin max(0.02, 0.5|di-dj|)) makes candidates with larger dead-reckoned trajectory deviation get higher cosine cost to the goal; plus a rollout anchor on GT actions.

CEM planning: 128 candidates from a unicycle prior with AR(1) noise, top-4 elites, 6 iterations, horizon 6, context 4; cost is 1 − cosine between pooled predicted final embedding and goal embedding; receding-horizon replanning.
ACT (negative-result variant): InfoNCE on pooled rollouts with cross-scene / temporal-permutation action negatives, τ=0.1, weight 0.25.
Real-robot deployment: model runs on a Jetson AGX Orin, predicted waypoints are sent to ROS 2 Nav2 (DWB) on a Husky A200 with progressive sub-goal fallback.

setting.backbone: Frozen DINOv2-ViT-S/14 or DINOv3-ViT-S/16 encoder + trainable 6-layer AdaLN ViT predictor (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: GNM navigation dataset (60+ hours, six robots), images and odometry actions only; evaluated on a held-out split of 1,316 trajectories
setting.observation: monocular RGB history (4 context frames) + goal image
setting.action_space: continuous SE(2) displacement sequences (dx, dy, sin/cos dθ) chosen by CEM; waypoints on the robot
setting.simulator: none (offline GNM dataset evaluation); real robot
setting.privileged: none at test time (odometry used only for training action labels; ground-truth trajectories used for the evaluation metrics)

numbers.extra: K=6 horizon, C=4 context, CEM planning; Base rollout + MCR phase
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (GNM test results), row Ours (DINOv2) MCR

numbers_note: Real-world results are only qualitative plus 5 trials (WorldModel 5/5 vs OmniVLA 2/5 success). Metrics are open-loop trajectory errors (AOE, MAOE, ADE, MADE), not SR/SPL.
results: On the GNM test split, MCR (DINOv2) gets AOE 7.63°, MAOE 11.11° and MADE 1.64 m, the best among all methods, narrowly beating OmniVLA (img) (7.73°/11.58°/1.72 m); ADE 0.99 is slightly behind NoMaD's 0.88. It cuts AOE 2.7× versus same-encoder DINO-WM (20.27°) and beats NWM (14.57°).
limitations: Evaluation is on open-loop trajectory error on a GNM held-out set; the real-world test is small (5 trials) and qualitative, in static or low-traffic scenes.
The goal-proximity cost ignores dynamic agents, and autoregressive error still compounds at long horizons.
The real-robot pipeline relies on lidar-based Nav2 for obstacle avoidance, and the ACT negative result is explained without a full mechanistic analysis.
